title: Particles
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry adventure on particle model and changes of state.
final_note: You walked through the particle model and changes of state.

concepts.def: Liquid to gas at bp; energy

walkthroughs.body_html:
Particles in a solid vibrate; in a liquid slide past each other; in a gas move freely.

Forces between particles weaken from solid to gas.

During a state change temperature is constant.

Energy goes into overcoming forces between particles.

Gas particles collide with container walls -> pressure.

More particles or higher temperature -> higher pressure.

mcqs.q: Pressure of a gas increases when:
When water boils, what is broken?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
